# The v13.2 launch playbook: the demo-first release sequence that produces measured strangers

> Rewritten 2026-09-24 by the assignee on the author's hand-over ([comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/14790#issuecomment-5818974455)). The earlier text is in the edit history.

## Context

The win condition stands: **traction, or revenue sufficient for the frontier tier.** The ROADMAP puts this playbook on the 13.2 path. Cornerstone 6's done signal is *"notes staged for the cut; the launch playbook's gates named and dated"*.

This body names each gate and dates it relative to **T**, the day 13.2.0 is cut. T is the operator's call. Once it is set it is recorded here, and every date below becomes a calendar date. **T = 2026-10-11** (UTC): 13.2.0 reached npm `latest` and its [release page](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/releases/tag/13.2.0) at 22:37Z.

Two things changed since the first version:
- **The measurement gate is gone.** The series this sequence was gated on was retired on 2026-07-05 (#14842; #14782 closed as not planned), because create-work does not wait on instruments. The baseline now comes from signals that already exist, and it never gates anything.
- **The FM outward door moved.** It belongs to the Institution line and is off the 13.2 path (see the ROADMAP's deferred set).

## The playbook

**Phase 0: Baseline (T−1; recorded, never a gate).** Read the free signals and record them here, together with N and M (see Phase 4):
- npm weekly downloads of `neo.mjs`;
- GitHub 14-day views and uniques, stars and forks;
- outside contributors with a merged PR in the last 30 days.

On 2026-09-24 they read:
- 3,583 downloads/week (09-15 to 09-21);
- 4,155 views and 920 uniques over 14 days;
- 3,282 stars and 241 forks;
- 4 outside contributors with 13 merged PRs.

These baselines include our own traffic. Thresholds are set against them, never against zero.

**Phase 1: The flagship, once (T = 2026-10-11).** All three parts of the gate must hold: **Gates 1 and 3 hold** (npm `latest` and the release page carry 13.2.0; the film is public). **Gate 2 holds (2026-10-12):** the first card in all four registries is the Workstation (id 27), behind a current cover. #19641 merged as `df478878a9` and pages#38 deployed as `5df4094` ([run 38239578535](https://github.com/neomjs/pages/actions/runs/38239578535)). Euclid's independent click-through reached the actual Workstation in all four modes ([receipt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/14800#issuecomment-6110852946)). My read-back confirms it from the other side: the four deployed catalogs the root Portal reads lead with id 27 at its per-mode URL, the choreography demo is last among visible cards, both covers match #19641's SHA-256s, and the production first card opens the Workstation UI. This supersedes my 00:09Z receipt, which proved that the card loads, not that it is the flagship (operator correction, 2026-10-12).
1. 13.2.0 is published: the release page and the npm package.
2. The site serves 13.2 with the docking demos current (the release gate). The first example card opens the Workstation in all four modes, behind a current cover. Card order ships inside the release package (#19425 replaced #17436's post-deploy flip, whose hourly data sync is gone); covers live in `neomjs/pages` `resources_pub/website/examples/`.
3. The film is published (#15252, cornerstone 4), recorded with its tour mode and #14780's motion standards.

What ships:
- one film;
- the live URL, meaning the Workstation and Dock Layouts on the 13.2 site;
- one "how it's built" post, which is the 13.2 notes' Dock chapter (#14800);
- one post on what Dock Layouts give a multi-window dashboard, carrying the film (#19602, from the operator's release-day goals).

Channels, in order:
1. **Canonical home, on T:** the 13.2.0 release page plus the portal's release view, SEO-first.
2. **X thread with the film, on T.**
3. **HN Show with the live URL, on the next weekday (Monday 2026-10-12).** Prepare for the "another JS thing?" objection with the one-runtime-many-windows differentiator.
4. **dev.to and r/javascript as syndication, after HN.**

**One flagship, not a barrage.** Using the engine needs no door of its own, because from T the published package is the call to action.

**Phase 2: The doors (no earlier than max(T+7, 2026-10-01) = 2026-10-18).** From this date the channels point strangers at contributing:
- **Contribute without a Brain.**
  - Gate: cornerstone 5's done signal (#18985): a good-first-issue supply, and a PR path a contributor completes without a Brain.
  - Hacktoberfest opens this door on 2026-10-01 on its own calendar. This phase decides only when the launch channels point at it.
- **Run the Agent OS locally.**
  - Gate: cornerstone 7's done signal (#14230): the supported local path reaches a running Agent OS without hand-edited config.
  - It joins the call to action in the week that signal holds, and never before this phase's date.

**Phase 3: Story beats (weekly from T+14 = 2026-10-25).** One beat a week, each linking back to the flagship:
- the 13.2 notes' other chapters, one per beat;
- the second public demo with its deterministic tour mode (cornerstone 4);
- last, the institution angle: the PRs here are written by a persistent agent team, with the evidence linked. The engine's notes tell the engine's story, so the organism's story gets its own beat.

A beat's gate is that its material is public and every claim in it links its evidence.

**Phase 4: The fold (T+7, T+14, T+21, T+28 = 2026-10-18, 10-25, 11-01, 11-08).**
- **Weekly comment.** Each week a comment on this ticket reads the Phase 0 signals against N and M:
  - **N** is the GitHub 14-day uniques at T+14 (2026-10-25).
  - **M** is the number of outside contributors with a merged PR by T+28 (2026-11-08).
- **No moving goalposts.** The owner sets N and M at T−1, and neither changes afterwards. **Frozen on 2026-10-11, before Phase 1: N = 2,500, M = 12** ([the T−1 reading](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/14790#issuecomment-6110573015)).
- **Destination.** The T+28 fold is the reach input to the post-release `/update-roadmap` round, which scopes the next release in `ROADMAP.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] T is recorded here once the operator sets it. No phase goes out before its date or before its named gate holds.
- [ ] The flagship film is recorded with its tour mode and #14780's motion standards.
- [x] N and M are recorded here before Phase 1, taken from the Phase 0 baseline.
- [ ] The T+28 fold lands as the reach input to the post-release `/update-roadmap` round.

## Out of Scope

- Pricing and packaging (the business repo).
- Paid promotion.
- The demos' implementation (their own leaves).
- Building reach instruments. That is a follow-up beat at most, never a gate.
- The FM outward door (#15519). #15526's composition ([comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/14790#issuecomment-5070246357)) binds the Institution line's launch, not 13.2.

## Bound FM outward-door slice — neomjs/neo#15526 composition

This is neomjs/neo#15526's composition **into** the existing phase 0→4 playbook, not a competing launch sequence. `<canonical site URL>` remains a symbolic slot until neomjs/neo#15520/#15523 bind the product name and site; no channel invents a substitute.

| Existing phase | FM outward-door moment | Bound gate / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **0 — instrument** | Instrument the canonical site's recorded-take funnel: hero view, play/complete, provenance-open, notify-me, then later download-select/resolve. | The existing neomjs/neo#14782 reach gate remains first. Before activation there is no download event or DOM action. |
| **1 — flagship, once** | Host the 90-second fusion take as the site's hero with replayable-test provenance. Every outward channel cites the **same site URL**; native media may preview, but the sole CTA is the site. | The engine repository is a first-screen proof link inside the site, never a competing outbound target. |
| **2 — stranger path** | Before row 3, offer **watch the fleet** and **notify me** only. After the packaged-shell first-self-use receipt, add exactly one download action resolving to the monorepo release receipt. | neomjs/neo#15490 row 3 walked via its named neomjs/neo-agent-brain#90 vehicle + neomjs/neo#15526 Contract Ledger complete + release receipt present. Until all three hold, the action is absent—not disabled or “coming soon.” |
| **3 — story beats** | Route identity-continuity, recovery, and subsequent product stories through the canonical site. | Each claim stays evidence-linked and folds into the same flagship funnel. |
| **4 — fold** | Carry stranger sessions, completed first runs, and their falsifying queries into neomjs/neo#14788's weekly weighting round. | N/M remain set from the phase-0 baseline; no post-hoc thresholds. |

The executable consumer/download boundary now lives in [#15526's T3 Contract Ledger](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/15526). Its “pricing” is operational auth/rate/resource cost, so neomjs/neo#14790's commercial-pricing out-of-scope boundary remains intact.

Current gate truth at publication: neomjs/neo#15520 and neomjs/neo#15523 are open; neomjs/neo#15490 row 3 is still first-self-use unwalked. The composition is live, but download activation is not.

**So the flagship shipped and the sequence meant to launch it is blocked on an instrument nobody is building.** That is the concrete stall, and it has been sitting for two months.

**The cancellation was a decision, not an oversight**, which is why re-opening `#14782` would be the wrong move. From `#14842`, recording the operator's verdict of 2026-07-05 that retired epic `#14564` and its measurement sub-series:

> *"Agent OS ships into client clouds without us, so install-measurement harnesses measure deployments we have no access to, and the framing **gated CREATE-work behind measurement theater**."*

**That verdict lands on this body's spine, not just its citation.** Phase 0 is *"instrument before anything moves"*; Phase 2 gates the CTA on a harness; the first AC is *"no announcement before its instrument"*. That is the framing the operator called theater, written as the sequence's backbone. The stale `#14782` link is the symptom.

**What I would do, offered rather than done** — your ticket:

1. **Keep** the ordering, the channel sequence and the one-flagship-not-a-barrage discipline. None of that depends on measurement gating, and it is the genuinely useful part.
2. **Drop Phase 0 as a gate.** Reach instrumentation becomes a follow-up beat, not a precondition. The operator's verdict says create-work does not wait on it.
3. **Re-derive Phase 2's gate.** `#14230` (local-first onboarding, fork → install → try a lane → PR) survived the retirement and is CREATE-shaped; a TTFP harness against strangers' machines did not.
4. **Phase 4 and the N/M thresholds** need a destination that is not a July date — `#14788`'s scoping wave has passed.

I am not editing your body and I am not retiring anything. If you would rather hand the rewrite to me as the assignee, say so and I will bring you the text before it lands.

**One thing I am not claiming:** whether the launch sequence belongs in v13.2 at all after that re-scope. That is an operator call and I have not asked it.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-10-11T15:44:18Z

### Phase 1 drafts for the operator: the X thread on T, Show HN the next weekday

The voice is yours, so edit freely. Both follow D#19500's distribution read: the receipt (the film) rides in the post, and the links go in the first reply. Each claim matches the post (#19602) and the notes. The URLs resolve once the 13.2 pages deploy is live; I check them then.

**X thread** (every post fits in 280 characters, counting URLs at 23):

```
1/ [the film, uploaded natively]
Neo.mjs 13.2 is out. Its centerpiece: Dock Layouts across real browser windows. Drag a live pane out into its own OS window, carry it to another window, bring it home, then undo all of it. The pane stays the same component the whole way.

2/ (first reply: the links)
Try it in desktop Chrome: https://neomjs.com/dist/production/apps/workstation/index.html
Release notes: https://github.com/neomjs/neo/releases/tag/13.2.0
The post: https://neomjs.com/news/blog/blog/multi-window-dashboards-with-dock-layouts

3/
No state is synced between windows. The app runs in a SharedWorker every window connects to, so a window only renders, and a pane in a popup is the same object in the same heap. 13.2 adds the dock: one arrangement document, one reducer, one undo history across windows.

4/
For a developer, a workspace starts as two configs: panes (ordinary component configs) and zones (where they start). Splitters, tabs, edge rails, drop targets, maximize and named perspectives come from the engine. Windows are an opt-in on top.

5/
The bounds: windows need SharedWorkers, so one origin. The browser decides when a window may open. The real-window runs were measured on Chrome.
```

**Show HN** (Mon 2026-10-12; title 80 characters):

```
Title: Show HN: Neo.mjs 13.2 – tear a live pane out into a real browser window and back
URL:   https://neomjs.com/dist/production/apps/workstation/index.html

First comment:
Hi HN, I'm the creator of Neo.mjs. The centerpiece of 13.2 is Dock Layouts across real browser windows. In the Workstation (the link; desktop Chrome), drag a tab past the window's edge and it becomes its own OS window mid-drag. Drag it over another window of the app and it joins it. Close a popup and its panes come home. Undo walks the arrangement across all the windows.

How it works: a Neo.mjs app runs in an App Worker, off the main thread. With SharedWorkers on, every window of the app connects to the same App Worker and only renders, so a pane in a popup is the same component instance, not a synced copy. The dock keeps each workspace's arrangement in one serialisable document. Every change is one operation through one reducer, and a move between windows commits both windows' documents in one transaction. That is what makes undo work across windows.

Limits: it needs SharedWorkers (one origin); the browser's pop-up permission decides when a window may open; we measured the real-window paths on Chrome.

Release notes: https://github.com/neomjs/neo/releases/tag/13.2.0
How it's used, with screenshots and code: https://neomjs.com/news/blog/blog/multi-window-dashboards-with-dock-layouts
Repo: https://github.com/neomjs/neo
```

The phases' calendar dates go into the body together with T, once 13.2.0 is on npm.
